question: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & a \\ -a & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, compute $(A')^2$ and show its relation to the identity matrix.
explanation:
First, $A' = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -a \\ a & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Now compute $(A')^2$:

$= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -a \\ a & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -a \\ a & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix} (0\times0 + -a\times a) & (0\times -a + -a\times 0) \\ (a\times 0 + 0\times a) & (a\times -a + 0\times 0) \end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix} -a^2 & 0 \\ 0 & -a^2 \end{bmatrix}$.

So $(A')^2 = -a^2 I$.
